summary: Serialized task-queue (Celery) drops per-action idempotency metadata -> duplicate tool executions across Python orchestration and Go webhook
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate downstream tool (webhook) executions when using Redwood Python SDK function-calling via a background task queue (Celery). The orchestration enqueues job payloads containing the SDK request/response state; when Celery serializes/deserializes the Celery message the per-action idempotency token is being lost or truncated leading to multiple invocations for the same logical function call. Impact: duplicates produce duplicate writes to customer downstream systems (billing ledger), intermittent data corruption, and urgent need for a rollback or compensation. Environment: Dedicated Redwood Private deployment behind an HSM-signing edge that rewrites an auth header; Celery worker pool (RabbitMQ broker) serializes tasks as JSON, Python 3.11, redwood-python-sdk v1.8.2. Timeline: 2026-03-09 18:22 UTC first reported by customer; they observed 4 duplicate webhook invocations for what should have been a single function-call.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a simple function/tool (POST webhook) that records incoming requests to an append-only log.

2) From a web frontend call server-side Python code that uses redwood-python-sdk to invoke function-calling; include per-action idempotency metadata (x-rw-idempotency: <uuid>) in the SDK call metadata.
3) Enqueue the SDK call payload into Celery (JSON serialization) and acknowledge the incoming HTTP request immediately; Celery worker later deserializes and executes the SDK call.
4) Observe the webhook receiving duplicate invocations for identical logical action IDs (same payload but different sequence numbers on Redwood logs).
logs: 2026-03-09T18:22:11Z WARN celery.serialize dropped header x-rw-idempotency (length=64 -> truncated to 32)
redwood-serving-runtime trace_id=tr-7bbf: mapped request -> model redwood/gptx-4-mini, funcall_id missing-idempotency-token -> accepted and executed
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Celery JSON serializer is truncating or dropping non-standard HTTP header metadata when pickling/logging the SDK call context, causing the serving runtime to treat calls as distinct.

Confirmed reproduction in customer sandbox when Celery serializer set to 'json' with custom header baggage. When using 'pickle' worker the header was preserved (customer cannot use pickle in prod for security reasons).

Observed that Private deployment includes an HSM edge that rewrites Authorization and signs a custom header (x-rt-sign) which sometimes splits long headers into two segments; downstream proxy collapsed segments resulting in truncated idempotency header.
Serving runtime logs show requests arriving without x-rw-idempotency header -> runtime assigns new per-action nonce and executes function call again.

Tested OK: patching SDK to embed an idempotency token inside the function-call payload (body) prevents duplicates — but this requires application change and exposes token in request body to downstream webhook (not desired for security/interpretation concerns).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:05 - Aisha Turner (Support): Thanks for the detailed report. We've flagged this as P1 due to duplicate side effects. Attaching initial logs and repro steps. Assigning to Marco for deep-dive.

2026-03-10 11:37 - Marco Diaz (SRE): Investigating. Early thought: serialization boundary is stripping header. Can customer share Celery config and exact header length/content? Any proxy/middleware that might rewrite multi-line headers?

2026-03-10 14:12 - Customer Engineer (ClipMate): We use default JSON serializer, RabbitMQ 3.11, and an edge HSM proxy that adds x-rt-sign. Idempotency token is a 64-char base64 string generated by SDK. Attached proxy logs showing header rewrite behavior.

2026-03-11 02:27 - Marco Diaz (SRE): Reproduced locally with a stub HSM proxy that splits long headers across multiple header frames. Confirmed that when header split occurs, upstream HTTP client library collapses frames and may truncate when reserializing into Celery JSON payload. Next steps: propose SDK change to persist idempotency token in the task payload metadata field that Celery will not mutate, and add server-side fallback that accepts an embedded token in an application-level field (x-rw-embedded-idempotency) for Private deployments.

2026-03-12 08:04 - Solutions Engineer (Nina Park): Workaround documented for customer: 1) shorten idempotency tokens to <=32 chars (temporary), 2) configure Celery to use kombu's 'pickle' only if acceptable, or 3) set SDK option to include 'idempotency' in function_call.arguments under an encrypted key. Engineering will provide SDK patch PR for review.

2026-03-12 12:30 - Customer Engineer (ClipMate): Applied token-length reduction and saw immediate reduction in duplicates in the last 24h. Still would like a robust SDK/server fix so we don't have to change token format.

2026-03-12 16:55 - Marco Diaz (SRE): Created draft PR to redwood-python-sdk to add safe serialization option (preserve_idempotency_in_payload=true). Also opened ticket with Private infra to check HSM proxy header fragmentation behavior and to consider passthrough mode for x-rw-idempotency headers.
2026-03-12 18:10 - Aisha Turner (Support): Marking follow-up items for Engineering and Private infra. Keeping ticket open while SDK PR and proxy config change are validated.
resolution: Mitigation and planned fixes: 1) Temporary customer workaround applied (shorten idempotency tokens to <=32 chars) and reduced duplicate rate. 2) SDK change: redwood-python-sdk will add a safe-serialization flag to embed per-action idempotency into the task payload (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/rewood-python-sdk/pull/412). 3) Server-side fallback: Add acceptance of application-level embedded idempotency header (x-rw-embedded-idempotency) for Private deployments during rollout window. 4) Private infra: investigate HSM proxy header fragmentation and add passthrough mode for x-rw-idempotency. Follow-ups: engineering to complete SDK patch and test cross-language reproduction with Go SDK (due 2026-03-20). Customer to monitor duplicates; support will validate once PR is deployed to staging.
